lines:
Implements the 2026-11-25 amendment of aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy.

PROVIDER ANSWERS
- New provider_failure module classifies every answer before re-dispatch: spend/quota, rate limit, transient, authentication/configuration, context-too-large, refusal. Spend and auth end the pass on first observation with the provider's bounded text plus the setting to fix; rate limit honours Retry-After (now carried from the transport through ProviderError::HttpStatus) else bounded backoff, then ends with the text; context overflow keeps compact-once and records CompactAndRetry; everything else is reported and continues.
- The refusal guard counts a class, not bytes, so a rotating payload cannot outrun it. An accepted turn clears the streak.
- Each classified answer records class + provider text + reaction as context.provider-failure evidence; gateway failures put the provider's text in the span body; "Canonical model result settled." is gone as a failure body.
- Chat-scoped ProviderLimitRegistryV1: the first spend/quota observation stops every pass and sibling child in that Chat before they dispatch.

DELEGATION
- Terminal child statuses (completed/failed/cancelled/interrupted) are delivered to the delegating model as one bounded report; delivery keys are committed as context.subagent-report before dispatch, so a restart re-delivers instead of replaying. Inline/cancel results mark themselves delivered.
- A live child whose last committed sequence is older than the 300 s stall window is reported as a stall with child id, sequence and age.
- Every Agent pass path (plain, approval, resume; Suspended keeps children) closes in the same pass: live children of the terminating node are cancelled and their terminal frames committed.
- Settlement and cancellation report real counters (ChildJobHandle tracks live turns/sequence/tokens; cancelled_frame merges them).

RUN STATE
- Pass liveness: a per-pass watcher reports chat.stall with ageSeconds and lastCommittedSequence after 180 s without a commit, re-reporting every 300 s; it never ends the pass and stops with the pass. Wired on both pipeline pass paths. The durable event is in the Run's stream; the UI run badge itself is frontend-derived and not changed here.
- Restart recovery leaves a durable report: chat.recovery_completed carries lastCommittedSequence + closedSpanCount + previous panic report; the outcome_uncertain path commits chat.recovery_report with reason, last sequence and the previous exit.
- App-blank trail: a process panic hook writes a bounded one-line crash-report.json (reason, message, location, thread, last committed sequence) and recovery folds it in once, then clears it.

VERIFICATION
- 7 incident-topology tests (six children vs spend-limit 429): only one dispatch, every child ends with provider text, class/text/reaction recorded, pass closes. Plus rotating-payload class streak, auth no-retry, Retry-After wait, wait-budget exhaustion, delegation delivery, terminal close, 7 report-planner tests, 3 registry tests, 2 live-counter tests, 4 classifier tests, 2 stall-report tests, 3 crash-report tests. No clock-based waits in the incident proof.
- desktop lib suite 699 passed; the only failure is service::tool_plugins::frozen_mcp_transport..., reproduced on a clean stash before these changes. capability-host suite green (3 literals updated for the new HttpStatus field).

REMAINING (warning, not hidden)
- Auto-resume of an outcome_uncertain request without the user's Continue is NOT implemented. It conflicts with the same specification's own safety verdict in the recorded incident: execution.failed carries automaticReplayAllowed:false and the recovery path refuses to replay a request the provider may already have accepted. Automatically re-dispatching would risk paying twice for the same turn. The resume now carries the durable report (reason, last sequence, previous panic) instead of starting from scratch, but the dispatch still needs the user's Continue. A product decision is required before changing this: either allow bounded automatic replay of an uncertain request, or keep the explicit continue.
- Note: the amendment deliberately extends the terminal set beyond the older "three conditions" project rule (spend/auth end a pass); this is the newer normative text and what the task specifies.

## Incident

`chat.c4dbf38e958dce7a2926a61926b9b86628776d72`, project `C:\src\PragerKochbuch`, workflow `workflow.custom.11` v3, model Gemini 4 Neon (tier `quality`), 2026-11-25 19:21 → 22:14 local.

User task: audit the modern German translation of all 1,613 recipes against the 1920 original, rewrite archaic wording, extend the glossary. Outcome: **€20 spent, no merged result, no final answer**; the user stopped the run by hand 2 h 25 min after its last event and recovers the artefacts in a new chat.

## What the history actually shows

1. **19:32:17 — the app went blank and had to be restarted.** On restart the harness committed `span.failed` + `execution.failed` with `status: outcome_uncertain` ("The provider may have accepted the request, but no conclusive terminal evidence was durably committed. Automatic replay is forbidden.") and `chat.recovery_completed`. The only way forward was the user typing "continue", which re-dispatched the turn from scratch.
2. **447 model spans, two kinds of outcome.** 143 completed and each has a `span.usage` row. The other 304 failed: 297 with body `Canonical model result settled.`, 7 with `This attempt was interrupted.` — every one has `output: null` and **no `span.usage` row at all**. The real cause appears once, at agent level.
3. **The parent agent node ended at 19:47:42** — after ten refusals the pass stopped with the provider's own 429 text (`You exceeded your spend-based rate limit … refused this exact request 10 times in a row`), committing `span.failed` and `execution.failed`.
4. **The same guard did not stop the children.** Batch 02's child ran to **turn 118 with 107 consecutive failures** (19:44:24–19:47:38), batch 01 to turn 57, batch 04 to turn 50. At 19:47 there were **189 model calls and 6 tool calls in one minute**. The two loops do not share the same notion of "identical request", and a spend limit that one child observes did not stop its five siblings.
5. **Children outlived their parent, silently.** All six were marked `failed` at 19:47:36–19:49:10 — the last one 90 s after `execution.failed` — each with `finalText: null`, and **no terminal child status was ever delivered to a delegating agent as a tool result**. Their `run`/`agent_loop` spans stayed open; from 19:49:10 to 22:14:24 the chat committed no event at all, until the user's Stop cancelled 12 spans.
6. **Counters lie.** The 19:33:20 `tool.subagent_cancel` results report `modelTurns: 0, inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0` for children that had already run 6–8 model turns — the numbers a user reads to judge spend.
7. **Spend ledger vs. bill.** Recorded: 13,156,108 input / 613,393 output tokens across the 143 accepted calls (main 4.04 M / 64 k, children 9.11 M / 550 k). The 304 refused attempts are unaccounted; the invoice was €20.
8. **Deliverables.** `.tmp_audit/patches/` holds patch_01/02/04/05/06 (~804 of 1,613 recipes, 170 glossary candidates) plus batch 03 as three raw part files; `content.sqlite` was never written (`max(recipe.updated_at) = 2026-11-25T13:03:33Z`) and `validate_and_merge.py --apply` never ran. Recovering that work is out of scope here.

## Required behaviour

The norm is recorded in `aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy`, amendment 2026-11-25 ("a delegated child reports back, and a provider answer is classified"). This task implements it.

**Delegation**
- Every terminal child status (`completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`) reaches the delegating agent as one bounded tool result, committed as an event first so a restart re-delivers it.
- A child's failure never re-runs the child and never ends the delegating node; the delegating model decides.
- A child that stops producing events without a terminal status is reported as a **stall** (child id, last committed sequence, age of that sequence). No child holds a run open while its delegator hears nothing.
- When an agent node terminates for any reason, its live children are cancelled and their terminal statuses committed in the same pass: no span outlives the pass that owns it.

**Provider answers**
- A failure is classified before anything is re-dispatched: spend/quota limit (end the pass at once with the provider's text), rate limit (honour `Retry-After`, otherwise bounded backoff, then end with the text), transient (backoff retry), authentication/configuration (no retry, name the setting), context too large (compact once, then re-dispatch).
- A spend or quota limit is account-scoped: the first child that observes it stops every sibling dispatching to that provider in the same Chat, instead of six children each burning into the same wall.
- The class, the provider's bounded text and the chosen reaction are recorded on the attempt; `Canonical model result settled.` may never be a failure body again.
- The repeated-refusal guard counts a **class**, not a byte-identical payload, so a child cannot reach 107 refusals while its parent stops at 10.

**Run state**
- No run sits open with zero events: a stalled pass reaches a terminal status or raises a visible stall within a bounded time, and Run details shows failed/stalled rather than "running".
- Restart recovery leaves a durable report; an `outcome_uncertain` request resumes with it instead of needing a user "continue" and a fresh dispatch.
- A child's settlement and cancellation report its real `modelTurns`, `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`.
- The app-blank failure leaves a diagnostic trail that survives the restart (panic/exit reason, last committed sequence).

**Proof**
- A regression test reproduces the incident topology — six delegated children against a provider that answers 429 to every dispatch — and asserts: class-based reactions, provider text surfaced, the parent stops once, the first spend-limit observation stops the siblings, children are cancelled with their statuses delivered, every span closes, the history shows the failure. No clock-based waits.

## Constraints

- Do not re-run the recipe audit or touch `content.sqlite` as part of this work.
- Do not weaken invariant 4: no budget or counter may end a run, and an accepted turn clears the refusal count.

data.title: A refused or interrupted run must end visibly: no opaque retries, no silent hang, no lost outcome
